chunks: Ṣāliḥ ibn Mītham narrated from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
There is no man who bears false testimony against a Muslim in order to cut off his wealth except that Allah writes for him in its place a warrant to the Fire.

key_terms.النَّارِ: the Fire, meaning Hell as punishment
key_terms.شَهَادَةَ زُورٍ: false testimony given in deception and injustice
key_terms.مَالَهُ: his wealth or property that is being wrongfully taken
key_terms.مُسْلِمٍ: a Muslim whose rights and property are being violated

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about giving false testimony to seize a Muslim’s wealth?
ai.summary: This hadith condemns false testimony used to unlawfully deprive a Muslim of his property. It portrays such an act as a grave sin whose consequence is a written warrant to the Fire, showing the severe moral and legal weight of perjury and financial injustice.
